Years of high feed costs and a shrinking national cattle herd have driven beef prices to record or near-record levels. United States Department of Agriculture data shows that the herd is now at its smallest size since 1951.
Trump’s Executive Orders and Take on “Monopoly”

On Friday, Trump signed two executive orders: one that allows ranchers to self-process and sell their own products, and another that mandates country-of-origin labeling on foreign beef and pushes for the removal of gray wolf protections, among other things.
In addition, Trump said that meat processors, including

, have a “monopoly” on the industry. “I’ve heard all about it. I’ve been listening to it … and they say they’re a very nasty group, very difficult to deal with," said Trump. “And they cost our farmers a lot of money, and they cost our ranchers a lot of money, and they cost the public a lot of money in grief, and we’re not going to let it happen any longer.”
When asked about the timeline on the country-of-origin labeling, Trump said, “We’re putting it in front of Congress right away.”
